item.title: Eastern North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
889
ABPZ20 KNHC 290519
TWOEP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
1100 PM PDT Fri Aug 28 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Tropical
Storm Karina, located well southwest of the southern tip of the Baja
California Peninsula, and on Tropical Storm Lowell, located well
east-southeast of the Hawaiian Islands.

Well Offshore of Southwestern Mexico:
An area of disturbed weather, associated with a tropical wave, is
located well to the south of southwestern Mexico. Environmental
conditions appear favorable for gradual development of this system,
and a tropical depression is likely to form early next week while
it moves west-northwestward to northwestward at 10 to 15 mph.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...30 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...high...80 percent.

Central Pacific:
An area of low pressure could form well south or southwest of the
Hawaiian Islands in a few days. Some gradual development is possible
thereafter and a tropical depression could form during the middle
part of next week while the system moves slowly west-northwestward,
well offshore of the Hawaiian Islands.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...near 0 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...medium...40 percent.

$$
Forecaster Gibbs

BULLETIN
Tropical Storm Karina Advisory Number   7
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP112026
200 AM PDT Sat Aug 29 2026
 
...KARINA MAINTAINS STRENGTH WELL SOUTHWEST OF THE SOUTHERN TIP OF
THE BAJA CALIFORNIA PENINSULA...
...STILL EXPECTED TO INTENSIFY TO MAJOR HURRICANE...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 200 AM PDT...0900 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...14.7N 117.0W
ABOUT 730 MI...1180 KM SW OF THE SOUTHERN TIP OF BAJA CALIFORNIA
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...65 MPH...100 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...NW OR 310 DEGREES AT 12 MPH...19 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...989 MB...29.21 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 200 AM PDT (0900 UTC), the center of Tropical Storm Karina was
located near latitude 14.7 North, longitude 117.0 West. Karina is
moving toward the northwest near 12 mph (19 km/h), followed by a 
more westerly motion over the weekend.
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 65 mph (100 km/h) with higher
gusts. Strengthening is forecast during the next several days.
Karina is forecast to become a hurricane later today and could
become a major hurricane early next week.
 
Tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 230 miles (370 km)
from the center.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 989 mb (29.21 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
SURF:  Swells generated by Karina will begin to affect portions of
the coast of southwest Mexico and the Baja California Peninsula
this weekend.  These swells are likely to cause life-threatening
surf and rip current conditions. Please consult products from your
local weather office.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 800 AM PDT.
 
$$
Forecaster Pierce/Gibbs

item.title: Tropical Storm Karina Forecast Discussion Number 7
item.description:
Issued at 200 AM PDT Sat Aug 29 2026 
428 
WTPZ41 KNHC 290852
TCDEP1
 
Tropical Storm Karina Discussion Number   7
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP112026
200 AM PDT Sat Aug 29 2026

The overall structure of Karina has remained largely unchanged, with 
a fragmented convective band located over the southern semicircle. 
Moderate southwesterly vertical wind shear continues to impart a 
slight northward tilt to the vortex, with most of the deep 
convection located over and north of the low-level circulation 
center. The subjective Dvorak intensity estimate from TAFB is 
T3.5/55 kt, which aligns with the latest objective estimates from 
UW-CIMSS. Based on a blend of these data, the initial intensity is 
held at 55 kt.
 
Karina continues on a northwestward heading of about 310/10 kt, 
driven by a ridge of high pressure over the southwestern United 
States. The storm is expected to slow down and turn westward as a 
mid-level trough to the north breaks down this ridge, allowing the 
ridge over the central North Pacific to build southeastward and take 
over as the primary steering flow. The NHC track forecast closely 
follows the HCCA guidance, essentially remaining unchanged from the 
previous forecast. 

SHIPS guidance continues to show a favorable environment for Karina 
to intensify over the next 60 h. Driven by light wind shear, warm 
SSTs, and abundant atmospheric moisture, conditions are conducive 
for the storm to reach major hurricane status. This is further 
supported by the Google DeepMind ensemble mean, where over 80 
percent of members bring Karina to major hurricane intensity. Beyond 
the weekend, SHIPS diagnostics indicate that conditions will 
deteriorate, which should induce a weakening trend by early next 
week.

item.title: Tropical Storm Lowell Forecast Discussion Number 7
item.description:
Issued at 1100 PM HST Fri Aug 28 2026 
403 
WTPZ42 KNHC 290851
TCDEP2
 
Tropical Storm Lowell Discussion Number   7
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP122026
1100 PM HST Fri Aug 28 2026
 
There has been little change in Lowell's organization or intensity 
during the past several hours. Moderate easterly vertical wind shear 
continues to displace the bulk of the deep convection over and west 
of the low-level circulation center. While an earlier scatterometer 
pass showed slightly lower winds, a blend of the latest objective 
intensity estimates and the subjective Dvorak intensity estimate 
from TAFB supports holding the initial intensity at 40 kt for this 
advisory.

The cyclone continues to move slowly westward, with an initial 
motion of about 280/7 kt. A low- to mid-level ridge is forecast to 
strengthen north of the cyclone during the next couple of days, 
which should cause Lowell to continue westward with a gradual 
increase in forward speed. This general westward motion is expected 
to continue through the weekend and into early next week. Track 
forecast uncertainty increases considerably thereafter due in part 
to the potential influence of Tropical Storm Karina to the northeast 
on Lowell's steering flow. There remains considerable spread in the 
guidance, particularly in forward speed, with the multi-model 
consensus (HCCA) and Google DeepMind ensemble mean generally faster 
than the GFS and ECMWF solutions. In addition to the along-track 
spread, the cross-track spread also increases considerably by day 5. 
Given these differences, the latest NHC track forecast has been 
nudged slightly southward and reflects a blend of the previous 
forecast and the latest HCCA and Google DeepMind ensemble mean.

The easterly vertical wind shear currently affecting Lowell is 
forecast to persist into the weekend, then steadily decrease by 
Sunday night into Monday, which should allow the cyclone to become 
better organized and gradually strengthen. However, the current 
sheared structure and nearby mid- to upper-level dry air should 
temper the rate of intensification in the short term. Environmental 
conditions are forecast to become more favorable thereafter, and a 
faster rate of strengthening is possible by early next week. The 
intensity forecast becomes more uncertain later in the period due to 
Lowell's potential interaction with Karina. A faster westward track 
would likely keep the cyclones sufficiently separated and allow 
Lowell to continue strengthening, while a slower solution could 
expose Lowell to stronger shear associated with outflow from Karina. 
The latest NHC intensity forecast is essentially unchanged from the 
previous advisory and lies near the middle of the guidance envelope.
